description: HTTP-layer acceptance scenarios (SPEC.md §8, §10, plus DNS/RES rules that need a behavioral rather than data-driven test). Unlike the data vectors, these are scenario specs: the test suite implements each as a test named with its id. Unless stated, the setup is: one valid key K1 = 'dh_' + 32 base62 chars whose SHA-256 is in API_KEY_HASHES; in-memory store; fake DNS with example.com fully configured (valid SPF/DMARC/MX); limits 10/min, 200/day.

vectors.input: GET /v1/domain/check?domain=example.com with Authorization: Bearer K1
vectors.expect: 200; Content-Type application/json; charset=utf-8; body validates against DomainCheckResult; domain == 'example.com'; checked_at parses as ISO-8601 UTC (ends in Z).

vectors.input: GET check for a domain whose fake DNS is empty (nonexistent)
vectors.expect: 200 (not 404); domain_exists false; summary.status 'fail'.

vectors.input: POST /v1/domain/check with valid key
vectors.expect: 405; error.code 'method_not_allowed'; header Allow: GET.

vectors.input: HEAD /v1/domain/check?domain=example.com with valid key
vectors.expect: 200; same headers as GET; empty body.

vectors.input: GET /v1/health with no auth header
vectors.expect: 200; body exactly {status:'ok', version:<package version>}; version equals SPEC.md version; the fake resolver records zero calls.

vectors.input: GET /v1/nope with valid key
vectors.expect: 404; body validates against Error; error.code 'not_found'; request_id present.

vectors.input: Any request without X-Request-Id
vectors.expect: Response header X-Request-Id is 32 lowercase hex chars; equals body.request_id.

vectors.input: Request with X-Request-Id: abc-123
vectors.expect: Response X-Request-Id == 'abc-123'.

vectors.input: Request with X-Request-Id: '<script>' and one with a 65-char value
vectors.expect: Supplied value is ignored; a generated 32-hex id is returned instead.

vectors.input: Each of: 200 check, 400, 401, 404, 429, health
vectors.expect: Every response has Cache-Control: no-store.

vectors.input: Fake resolver throws a non-DNS exception (e.g. TypeError) from inside a check
vectors.expect: 500; error.code 'internal_error'; body contains no stack trace, no 'TypeError', no file paths.

vectors.input: GET check with no Authorization and no X-API-Key
vectors.expect: 401; error.code 'missing_api_key'; header WWW-Authenticate: Bearer.

vectors.input: GET check with X-API-Key: K1 (no Authorization header)
Authorization: Bearer dh_wrongwrongwrongwrongwrongwrongwr
vectors.expect: 401; error.code 'invalid_api_key'; header WWW-Authenticate: Bearer.

vectors.input: GET /v1/domain/check?domain=example.com&api_key=K1 with no header
vectors.expect: 400; error.code 'key_in_query'; message mentions the Authorization header.

vectors.input: GET check with valid key AND ?key=K1 in query
vectors.expect: 400 key_in_query (rejected even though the header key is valid).

vectors.input: Run scripts/issue-key 100 times
vectors.expect: Every key matches ^dh_[A-Za-z0-9]{32}$; all unique; printed hash equals sha256(key) hex; key printed once.

vectors.input: Inspect configured key source and memory store after a successful request
vectors.expect: No plaintext key appears in the key source, the store, or any log line; only hashes.

vectors.input: Successful request with K1; capture log output
vectors.expect: Exactly one JSON line with event 'request'; key_id == first 12 hex of sha256(K1); fields ts, request_id, endpoint, status, summary_status, latency_ms, dns_queries present.

vectors.input: Invalid key making 15 requests in a minute
vectors.expect: All 401; none 429 (unauthenticated requests do not consume or check rate limits).

vectors.input: Valid key making 10 requests with invalid domain, then 1 valid request in the same minute
vectors.expect: First 10 are 400; 11th is 429 (invalid-input requests count against the limit).

vectors.input: 11 valid requests within one minute (controllable clock)
vectors.expect: First 10 are 200; 11th is 429 'rate_limited' with Retry-After ≥ 1 and ≤ 60.

vectors.input: Advance clock 61 s after H-22
vectors.expect: Next request is 200.

vectors.input: 200 requests spread across the UTC day (respecting per-minute), then one more
vectors.expect: 201st is 429; Retry-After equals seconds until next UTC midnight (±1).

vectors.input: Two different keys each send 10 requests in a minute
vectors.expect: All 20 are 200 (limits are per key).

vectors.input: Configure limits 3/min via config
vectors.expect: 4th request in a minute is 429 (limits are config, not constants).

vectors.input: First and second valid request of the day
vectors.expect: X-RateLimit-Limit 200; X-RateLimit-Remaining 199 then 198; X-RateLimit-Reset == next UTC midnight in Unix seconds. Headers also present on 400 and 429 responses for authenticated callers.

vectors.input: Store implementation that throws on every call
vectors.expect: Valid request still returns 200; log lines include 'store_unavailable' and/or 'usage_write_failed'; X-RateLimit-* headers are omitted (RL-3).

vectors.input: Requests for domain 'secretclient-example.com' using K1 from a client IP header 203.0.113.9; capture ALL log output
vectors.expect: No log line contains 'secretclient', K1, '203.0.113.9', or 'Bearer'.

vectors.input: K1: 3 successful checks on day 1, 1 failed (400) on day 1, 2 successful on day 3
vectors.expect: Store shows K1 counts {day1: 3, day3: 2}; active days {day1, day3}; the 400 is not counted as a successful check.

vectors.input: Store seeded: K1 active days 1 and 3; K2 active day 2 only; K3 active days 2,2 (same day twice). Run usage-report for days 1–7.
vectors.expect: unique active keys 3; repeat keys 1 (K1 only); total successful checks equals seeded sum.

vectors.input: Run the entire test suite with outbound network disabled
vectors.expect: All tests pass; production resolver is only constructed in the Vercel adapter, never in core.

vectors.input: Fake resolver errors with codes ENODATA, ENOTFOUND, ESERVFAIL, ETIMEOUT, ECONNREFUSED, and an unknown code
vectors.expect: Classified as no_records, nxdomain, error, error, error, error respectively.

vectors.input: Fake resolver delays every response by 2.5 s; SPF chain needs 5 sequential lookups
vectors.expect: Request completes in ≤ ~9 s; lookups started after the 8 s budget resolve as error; response is 200 with summary.status 'incomplete' or 'fail', never a timeout/500.

vectors.input: Fake resolver delays apex TXT, _dmarc TXT and MX by 1 s each
vectors.expect: Total check time < 2 s (they ran concurrently).

vectors.input: Run every vector in spf/dmarc/mx/check.json; collect all issues
vectors.expect: Every issue has exactly {code, severity, check, message}; severity matches the §9 registry for that code; message is non-empty, contains no '*', '`', '#', or newline.

vectors.input: Enumerate every issue message template and limitation string
vectors.expect: No message contains deliver/safe/compliant/guarantee, except the limitation sentence containing 'not an email deliverability test'.
